physicalNotes: Radius 0.30384891 Jupiter radii from Hord et al. 2024 (2024AJ....167..233H), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....167..233H/abstract): 21,722.8 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.0362 Jupiter masses (the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated value (M-R relationship, its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html) times JPL's Jupiter GM. sources.period: ExoFOP, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname EXOFOP): P 15.15120508799 d
sources.shape: Hord et al. 2024 (2024AJ....167..233H), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname HORD_ET_AL__2024): a/R* 47.003097; Hord et al. 2024 (2024AJ....167..233H), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname HORD_ET_AL__2024): inclination derived from its transit duration 2.5830151 h and Rp/R* 0.07777485 with its a/R* 47.003097 (Winn 2010, eqs. 14 and 16)
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: ExoFOP, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname EXOFOP): transit mid-time 2458909.543414 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 28 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
